🇲🇽📉 <u>Mexican Inflation Holds Near Banxico's 3% Target</u>

Mexico's annual headline inflation came in at 3.26% in its latest reading, with core inflation rising just 0.08% for the fortnight — below the 0.14% markets expected, El Economista reports from INEGI data. The number held near Banxico's 3% target even with onion up 19% and eggs up nearly 8%.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>Mexico City Bids to Be the World Capital of Sports Tourism</u>

Mexico City drew over 9 million hotel guests in the first half of 2026 — up 7% — while major events generated 60 billion pesos in economic impact and the sector grew 28% in a year, the city reported at the 4th World Sports Tourism Congress. More than 12 million people joined public activities during the World Cup, and the F1 Grand Prix is next on the calendar.

🇲🇽🕊️ <u>Homicides Down 53% — Lowest August in 12 Years</u>

Daily homicides in Mexico fell from 86.9 to 40.8 between September 2024 and August 2026 — a 53% drop, and the lowest August in a 12-year series, per the SESNSP. The homicide rate per 100,000 fell 49%, violent vehicle theft dropped 54%, and 30 of 32 states improved, led by San Luis Potosí at −80%. "El promedio de 40.8 homicidios diarios es el menor observado," said security official Marcela Figueroa.

🇲🇽📚 <u>Mexico Holds Steady on PISA as the OECD Slides</u>

While the OECD average fell 22 points in math and 28 in reading over the decade, Mexico held its ground in reading and science on PISA 2025 — after expanding coverage to more vulnerable students without widening the gap. Even the OECD's own Andreas Schleicher conceded: "México ha mostrado resiliencia."

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Mexico Pours 107 Billion Pesos Into Its Farmers</u>

Mexico is channeling 107 billion pesos to 13 million producers this year through 10 federal programs across 2,470 municipalities, SADER reports. Bean output reached 1.36 million tons — 300,000 above target and into self-sufficiency — while a new accord guarantees a "fair price" for national white corn.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Hits Record 22.8 Million Formal Jobs</u>

Mexico closed August with 22,798,473 registered formal jobs — the highest ever for an August and the second-highest on record, the IMSS reported. A record 19.86 million are permanent positions, and the average base wage rose to 673.1 pesos per day.

🇲🇽💰 <u>2027 budget: no new taxes, 43 million kept covered</u>

Hacienda delivered Mexico's 2027 economic package to Congress: 10.6 trillion pesos in spending, growth pegged at up to 2.5%, and the deficit trimmed to 3.9% of GDP — fiscal consolidation with no new taxes. Social programs are locked in at 2.6% of GDP, reaching roughly 43 million people. The plan assumes a 3% inflation rate, a peso at 18.6 to the dollar, and oil at 54.7 dollars a barrel. (El Financiero)

🛰️🇲🇽 <u>Mexico and US down cartel drones over the border</u>

Mexico and the US launched Operativo Águila Alta to knock cartel surveillance drones out of the sky over the Tijuana-San Diego corridor — each country operating strictly within its own territory. Sedena deployed 165 specialized anti-drone units under Gen. Ricardo Trevilla, after US forces downed roughly 100 drones in the sector. Coordination, not subordination.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena rejects US-'witness' smear against senator</u>

After N+ reported that Morena senator Julieta Ramírez had signed a preliminary deal to act as a 'witness' for US authorities, she hit back: 'I demand that N+ produce the document I supposedly signed.' Morena's Ariadna Montiel backed her — 'the accusations are false; I believe Julieta, she's a very responsible young woman' — dismissing it as a manufactured black campaign against a figure eyeing Baja California's governorship.

📚🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's illiteracy rate hits a record-low 3.8%</u>

Mexico cut illiteracy from 4.1% to 3.8% in a single year — the lowest rate in the country's history. Under the National Literacy Strategy, more than 277,000 adults learned to read and write, while 323,000 finished primary school and 542,000 finished secondary. Education Secretary Mario Delgado called it 'one of the deepest acts of justice, equity and love there is.'
